title: Singing the Pima song 'Water Babies'
summary: Moore offers to sing a chant Skomuck taught him, explains its meaning, and sings it; he links it to learning projection from Buster Bailey, Red Allen and Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So, you learned your tribal songs and a -- and even the dances first. And that carried you a -- into when you started school you were able to play musical and various instruments, any pipes, or did you have an early beginning of an education in music at that time?
A--, yes. Would you like a sample of what the songs that Skomuck taught me in my early years?
Would you like a little taste of the Pima?
Yea! That would be very good!

Oh, thank you. The title of this song is "Schulduck Mahmu " -- translated in English it's "Water Babies", and it describes how the little birds along the Gila River when they used to have water. Of course it's a wash now. They'd -- they'd be flying low over the water, drinking it or bathing in it -- the little birds -- and that's the song about the birds. And this is the way it goes.

Very beautiful. That's -- I'm sure that a song like that and a -- and a kind of a melody and the flavor that that melody has has appeared in some of your work as you became a professional musician. Would you feel -- do you feel that some of that a, that feeling and that melody has come up in things that you've played over the years in various orchestras when you've been playing with people like Buster Bailey and Henry "Red" Allen?

Oh yes, yes, yes, yes. I learned the art of projection -- to project to the listeners in the audience by watching the great musicians that I have worked with. As you say Buster Bailey and "Red" Allen and Louis Armstrong and many, many greats that I can't a -- I could mention, I mean in the short space of time like we -- like here. I have worked with many. I've learned how to, how to get that rhythm and also the blues and sing things like "Basin Street", "Saint James Infirmary". And some on my albums are -- are on the albums when I made them. And a -- I had quite a lot of fun doing a, doing -- learning the process of how to project and listen to other people sing -- that's the way I learned. I think everybody learns by listening to other people. I always loved to hear either Jack Teagarden or a, or a -- any of the big bands or big name musicians that a -- and there are some musicians that are lesser known, that are not -- haven't been found yet that you can -- sometimes you go into clubs and listen to. And

you learn a few things from somebody that is unknown. You'd be surprised how many I've listened to that I have never heard name mentioned before, and you know who they are. I go to a club; I listen, and I get things like that.
